# Current behavior that was noticed while building the corpus and has NOT been
# decided on. Each case here pins what the Go engine does today so that a
# change is deliberate and visible, not accidental. When a behavior is fixed
# on purpose, delete its case here and add the intended one to the proper file.
#
# Flagged for a decision:
#   - "inf", "nan", "Infinity" and "-inf" read as number literals, not symbols
#     (the lexer tries ParseFloat first), and "1_000" / "+5" are numbers too.
#   - (number ...) accepts the same forms.
#   - (nth ...) and (range ...) silently truncate fractional arguments.
#   - (/ x) with one argument returns x, not 1/x.
#   - (pow -8 1/3) yields NaN instead of an error.
#   - (exit ...) inside a function that a builtin calls (map/filter/fold) is
#     reported as an error instead of ending the script with that value —
#     the signal is wrapped by the builtin's error context and lost.
#   - str-fmt leaks Go formatting (recorded in strings.txt, its own pack).

=== inf literal
inf
--- want
(number "inf")

=== negative inf literal
-inf
--- want
(- 0 (number "inf"))

=== nan literal
nan
--- want
(number "nan")

=== Infinity literal
Infinity
--- want
(number "inf")

=== underscore digit separator literal
1_000
--- want
1000

=== plus sign literal
+5
--- want
5

=== number accepts inf
(number "inf")
--- want
(/ 1e308 1e-308)

=== number accepts underscore separator
(number "1_000")
--- want
1000

=== number rejects hex
(number "0x10")
--- error

=== hex literal is a symbol
0x10
--- error

=== nth truncates a fractional index
(nth (list 1 2) 1.5)
--- want
2

=== range truncates a fractional end
(range 1.5)
--- want
(list 0)

=== range truncates a fractional start
(range 2.5 5)
--- want
(list 2 3 4)

=== unary division returns the argument
(/ 2)
--- want
2

=== pow of a negative base to a fractional exponent is NaN
(pow -8 (/ 1 3))
--- want
(number "nan")

=== exit inside a builtin-called function is an error
(map (fn (x) (exit 7)) (list 1 2))
--- error
